claim: CNS tumors represent more than 25% of cancer cases in children.
source: In contrast, they represent more than 25% of cancer cases in children (including medulloblastoma, retinoblastoma, rhabdoid tumors (AT/RT), gliomas etc), suggesting that the developing CNS is particularly sensitive to malignant transformation (Arora et al., 2009; Curado et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Arora et al., 2009 and Curado et al., 2007.

claim: CNS tumors constitute less than 2% of all cancers in adults.
source: Central nervous system (CNS) tumors are rare and constitute less than 2% of all cancers in adults.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact in the manuscript text.

claim: The developing CNS is particularly sensitive to malignant transformation.
source: In contrast, they represent more than 25% of cancer cases in children (including medulloblastoma, retinoblastoma, rhabdoid tumors (AT/RT), gliomas etc), suggesting that the developing CNS is particularly sensitive to malignant transformation (Arora et al., 2009; Curado et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by the high percentage of CNS tumors in children and citations to Arora et al., 2009 and Curado et al., 2007.

claim: Pediatric tumors are often genetically stable.
source: Moreover, unlike most adult tumors, pediatric tumors are often genetically stable and their initiation and progression do not necessarily require the accumulation of mutations in multiple genes.
evidence: The claim is stated as a general characteristic of pediatric tumors.

claim: Biallelic inactivation of a single gene is sometimes sufficient to trigger malignant growth in pediatric tumors.
source: For example, the biallelic inactivation of a single gene is sometimes sufficient to trigger malignant growth as illustrated by mutations in the RB1 and SMARCB1 genes in retinoblastoma and rhabdoid tumors respectively (Biswas et al., 2016; Gröbner et al., 2018; Marshall et al., 2014; Puisieux et al., 2018; Scotting et al., 2005; Vogelstein et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by examples of RB1 and SMARCB1 mutations and multiple citations.

claim: CNS pediatric tumors such as medulloblastomas recapitulate the fetal transcription program that was active in the cell of origin.
source: Recent studies suggest that CNS pediatric tumors such as medulloblastomas recapitulate the fetal transcription program that was active in the cell of origin (Vladoiu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vladoiu et al., 2019.

claim: The Drosophila CNS arises from a small pool of asymmetrically-dividing neural stem cells called neuroblasts.
source: The Drosophila CNS arises from a small pool of asymmetrically-dividing neural stem cells (NSCs), called neuroblasts (NBs).
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about Drosophila CNS development.

claim: Neuroblasts possess a limited self-renewing potential.
source: NBs possess a limited self-renewing potential.
evidence: The claim is stated as a characteristic of neuroblasts.

claim: Neuroblasts divide all along development to self-renew while generating daughter cells named Ganglion Mother Cells (GMCs).
source: They divide all along development (embryonic and larval stages) to self-renew while generating daughter cells named Ganglion Mother Cells (GMCs) (Maurange and Gould, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Maurange and Gould, 2005.

claim: GMCs usually divide once to produce two post-mitotic neurons or glia.
source: GMCs then usually divide once to produce two post-mitotic neurons or glia.
evidence: The claim is stated as a characteristic of GMC behavior.

claim: Neuroblasts are the fastest cycling cells during development, able to divide every hour during larval stages.
source: NBs are the fastest cycling cells during development, able to divide every hour during larval stages when most of the neurons are produced (Truman and Bate, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Truman and Bate, 1988.

claim: All neuroblasts terminate during metamorphosis and are absent in adults.
source: However, all NBs terminate during metamorphosis and are absent in adults.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about neuroblast development.

claim: Imp and Syp are essential to first promote and then conclude the period of neuroblast activity.
source: Two antagonistic RNA-binding proteins, IGF-II mRNA-binding protein (Imp) and Syncrip (Syp) are essential to first promote and then conclude this formidable period of activity.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about the roles of Imp and Syp.

claim: During early larval development (L1/L2), neuroblasts express Imp that promotes NB self-renewal.
source: During early larval development (L1/L2), NBs express Imp that promotes NB self-renewal.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about Imp expression and function.

claim: Around late L2/early L3, neuroblasts silence Imp to express Syp that remains expressed until NB decommissioning during metamorphosis.
source: Around late L2/early L3, NBs silence Imp to express Syp that remains expressed until NB decommissioning during metamorphosis (Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2017.

claim: The Imp-to-Syp transition is essential to render neuroblasts competent to respond to subsequent pupal pulses of the steroid hormone ecdysone and initiate a last differentiative division.
source: This Imp-to-Syp transition is essential to render NBs competent to respond to subsequent pupal pulses of the steroid hormone ecdysone and initiate a last differentiative division (Homem et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Homem et al., 2014 and Yang et al., 2017.

claim: Failure to trigger the Imp-to-Syp transition results in neuroblasts permanently dividing in adults.
source: Failure to trigger the transition results in NBs permanently dividing in adults (Maurange et al., 2008; Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Maurange et al., 2008; Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; and Yang et al., 2017.

claim: The Imp-to-Syp transition appears to be mainly regulated by a NB intrinsic timing mechanism driven by the sequential expression of transcription factors.
source: The Imp-to-Syp transition appears to be mainly regulated by a NB intrinsic timing mechanism driven by the sequential expression of transcription factors (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2017; Syed et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2017; and Syed et al., 2017.

claim: Temporal transcription factors have been first identified for their ability to specify different neuronal fates produced by neuroblasts as they divide.
source: This series of factors, also known as temporal transcription factors, has been first identified for its ability to specify different neuronal fates produced by NBs as they divide (Bayraktar and Doe, 2013; Isshiki et al., 2001; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bayraktar and Doe, 2013; Isshiki et al., 2001; and Li et al., 2013.

claim: Temporal transcription factors schedule the Imp-to-Syp transition to ensure that neuroblasts will not continue cycling in adults.
source: In addition, temporal transcription factors also schedule the Imp-to-Syp transition to ensure that NBs will not continue cycling in adults.
evidence: The claim is stated as a function of temporal transcription factors.

claim: Perturbation of the asymmetric division process during early development can lead to neuroblast exponential amplification.
source: Perturbation of the asymmetric division process during early development can lead to NB exponential amplification.
evidence: The claim is stated as a consequence of perturbing asymmetric division.

claim: Serial transplantations of asymmetric division-defective neuroblasts have revealed an ability to proliferate for months, if not years, demonstrating tumorigenic characteristics.
source: Serial transplantations of asymmetric division-defective NBs have revealed an ability to proliferate for months, if not years, demonstrating tumorigenic characteristics (Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005.

claim: Perturbation of asymmetric divisions can be induced by the inactivation of the transcription factor Prospero (Pros) in type I NB lineages.
source: Perturbation of asymmetric divisions can be induced by the inactivation of the transcription factor Prospero (Pros) in type I NB lineages (most lineages in the ventral nerve cord (VNC) and central brain (CB)).
evidence: The claim is stated as a method to perturb asymmetric divisions.

claim: During development, Pros is strongly expressed in GMCs where it accumulates to induce cell cycle-exit and neuronal or glial differentiation.
source: During development, Pros is strongly expressed in GMCs where it accumulates to induce cell cycle-exit and neuronal or glial differentiation (Choksi et al., 2006; Hirata et al., 1995; Matsuzaki et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Choksi et al., 2006; Hirata et al., 1995; and Matsuzaki et al., 1992.

claim: GMCs that lack pros fail to differentiate and revert to a NB-like state, triggering rapid NB amplification at the expense of neuron production.
source: GMCs that lack pros fail to differentiate and revert to a NB-like state. This triggers rapid NB amplification at the expense of neuron production (Bello et al., 2006; Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bello et al., 2006 and Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005.

claim: Inactivation of pros in neuroblasts before mid-L3 leads to aggressive NB tumors that persist growing in adults.
source: We have previously shown that inactivation of pros in NBs, and their subsequent GMCs, before mid-L3 (L3 being the last larval stage) leads to aggressive NB tumors that persist growing in adults.
evidence: The claim is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claim: Inactivation of pros after mid-L3 leads to transient NB amplification and most supernumerary NB properly differentiate during metamorphosis, leading to an absence of growing tumors in adults.
source: In contrast, inactivation of pros after mid-L3 leads to transient NB amplification and most supernumerary NB properly differentiate during metamorphosis, leading to an absence of growing tumors in adults (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Propagation of NB tumor growth beyond normal developmental stages is caused by the aberrant maintenance of Imp and the transcription factor Chinmo from early-born GMCs.
source: Interestingly, propagation of NB tumor growth beyond normal developmental stages is caused by the aberrant maintenance of Imp and the transcription factor Chinmo from early-born GMCs, the latter representing the cells of origin of such aggressive tumors (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Chinmo and Imp positively cross-regulate and inactivation of either in NB tumors stops tumorigenic growth.
source: Chinmo and Imp positively cross-regulate and inactivation of either in NB tumors stops tumorigenic growth.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about the relationship between Chinmo and Imp.

claim: pros-/- NB tumors can only be induced during an early window of development.
source: Because pros-/- NB tumors can only be induced during an early window of development, and are caused by the biallelic inactivation of a single gene, they represent an exciting and simple model to investigate the basic mechanisms driving the growth of tumors with an early developmental origin, such as in the case of pediatric CNS cancers.
evidence: The claim is stated as a characteristic of pros-/- NB tumors.

claim: NB tumors can be induced from type II NBs upon inactivation of the NHL-domain family protein Brat.
source: NB tumors can also be induced from type II NBs (a small subset of NBs in the central brain) or from neurons upon inactivation of the NHL-domain family protein Brat or Nerfin-1 respectively (Bello et al., 2006; Betschinger et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2006) (Froldi et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bello et al., 2006; Betschinger et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2006; and Froldi et al., 2015.

claim: NB tumors can be induced from neurons upon inactivation of Nerfin-1.
source: NB tumors can also be induced from type II NBs (a small subset of NBs in the central brain) or from neurons upon inactivation of the NHL-domain family protein Brat or Nerfin-1 respectively (Bello et al., 2006; Betschinger et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2006) (Froldi et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bello et al., 2006; Betschinger et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2006; and Froldi et al., 2015.

claim: In different types of NB tumors, tumor growth appears to rely on the aberrant expression of the Chinmo/Imp module.
source: In both cases, tumor growth appears to rely on the aberrant expression of the Chinmo/Imp module arguing for a general tumor-driving mechanism in the developing Drosophila CNS (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Chinmo and Imp are only expressed in a subpopulation of cells in different types of NB tumors, demonstrating heterogeneity in the population of tumor NBs.
source: Interestingly, in the different types of NB tumors, Chinmo and Imp are only expressed in a subpopulation of cells, demonstrating heterogeneity in the population of tumor NBs (tNBs).
evidence: The claim is stated as an observation about Chinmo and Imp expression in tumors.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq was performed on 5740 cells with a median number of 1806 genes/cell.
source: Using the Chromium (10x Genomics) approach, we sequenced 5740 cells with a median number of 1806 genes/cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the single-cell RNA-seq experiment and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PC3, PC4 and PC7 identify the early and late larval NB temporal markers, Imp and Eip93F (E93), being expressed in different subsets of tNBs.
source: PC3, PC4 and PC7 in particular caught our attention, as they all identify the early and late larval NB temporal markers, Imp and Eip93F (E93) (Syed et al., 2017), being expressed in different subsets of tNBs (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCA analysis and reference to Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, with a citation to Syed et al., 2017.

claim: Early and late larval NB markers are major components defining cellular heterogeneity in NB tumors.
source: This indicates that early and late larval NB markers are major components defining cellular heterogeneity in NB tumors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the PCA analysis showing that Imp and E93 distinguish different subsets of tNBs.

claim: Graph-based clustering led to a UMAP representation composed of five main clusters and two smaller ones.
source: We next proceeded to graph-based clustering. This led to a UMAP representation composed of five main clusters and two smaller ones (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the clustering analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: NB identity genes like miranda (mira) or deadpan (dpn) appeared homogeneously distributed on the UMAP representation.
source: Consistently, NB identity genes like miranda (mira) or deadpan (dpn), appeared homogeneously distributed on the UMAP representation while genes defining cholinergic (VAChT), GABAergic (Gad1) and glutamatergic (VGlut) neurons were absent (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Genes defining cholinergic (VAChT), GABAergic (Gad1) and glutamatergic (VGlut) neurons were absent from the UMAP representation.
source: Consistently, NB identity genes like miranda (mira) or deadpan (dpn), appeared homogeneously distributed on the UMAP representation while genes defining cholinergic (VAChT), GABAergic (Gad1) and glutamatergic (VGlut) neurons were absent (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Pan-glial genes (repo) were not detected in the UMAP representation.
source: Similarly, pan-glial genes (repo) were not detected (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The two smaller clusters appear to be composed of tNBs expressing stress or growth arrest factors such as Gadd45, Irbp18, Xrp1 and GstE6.
source: The two smaller clusters appear to be composed of tNBs expressing stress or growth arrest factors such as Gadd45, Irbp18, Xrp1 and GstE6 possibly composing a sub-population of tNBs under cellular stress (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) (Akdemir et al., 2007; Francis et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis, reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, and citations to Akdemir et al., 2007; Francis et al., 2016; and Lee et al., 2018.

claim: Differential expression analysis identifies 'cluster 2' (1268 out of 5740 cells (22%)) as being strongly defined by the expression of the early NB temporal marker Imp.
source: Differential expression analysis identifies 'cluster 2' (1268 out of 5740 cells (22%)) as being strongly defined by the expression of the early NB temporal marker Imp (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by differential expression analysis and reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: E93 expression inversely correlates with Imp expression on the UMAP representation, being strongly expressed throughout all other clusters.
source: In contrast, E93 expression inversely correlates with Imp expression on the UMAP representation, being strongly expressed throughout all other clusters (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The presence of 4 large clusters (clusters 0, 1, 3, 4) within the E93 expression domain on the UMAP representation implies further cellular heterogeneity within the E93+ tNB population.
source: The presence of 4 large clusters (clusters 0, 1, 3, 4) within the E93 expression domain on the UMAP representation implies further cellular heterogeneity within the E93+ tNB population (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the presence of multiple clusters within the E93+ domain and reference to Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Oatp74D, SP1173, Plum, Gapdh2, Chd64, CG10939, CG44325, CG10512 and CG5953 distinguish the Imp+ identity in both NBs during development and tNBs in tumors.
source: We found that the genes encoding for the transmembrane transporters Oatp74D and SP1173, the Ig-superfamily transmembrane protein Plum, the glucose metabolism protein Gapdh2, the cytoskeleton protein Chd64, as well as CG10939, CG44325, CG10512 and CG5953 distinguish the Imp+ identity in both NBs during development and tNBs in tumors.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of gene expression in NBs during development and tNBs in tumors.

claim: The CDC25 gene string (stg), CG15628, CG15646 and the long non-coding RNA noe constitute a subset of genes whose transcription distinguishes the E93+ identity in both NBs during development and tNBs in tumors.
source: In contrast, the CDC25 gene string (stg), CG15628, CG15646 and the long non-coding RNA noe constitute a subset of genes whose transcription distinguishes the E93+ identity in both NBs during development and tNBs in tumors (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of gene expression in NBs during development and tNBs in tumors, with reference to Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: A subset of larval NB temporal patterning genes is redeployed in tumors defining various tNB states.
source: Thus, a subset of larval NB temporal patterning genes is redeployed in tumors defining various tNB states.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that genes distinguishing Imp+ and E93+ identities in development also distinguish these identities in tumors.

claim: chinmo mRNA is globally strongly expressed throughout all clusters.
source: Of note, chinmo mRNA is globally strongly expressed throughout all clusters (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: chinmo is post-transcriptionally regulated in NBs throughout development.
source: This is reminiscent of its known post-transcriptional regulation in NBs throughout development (Dillard et al., 2018; Zhu et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dillard et al., 2018 and Zhu et al., 2006.

claim: Forced transcription of a UAS-mCherrychinmoUTRs transgene in the tumor led to mCherry expression only in the tNBs that express the endogenous Chinmo.
source: Consistent with a post-transcriptional regulation of chinmo in tumors, we found that forced transcription of a UAS-mCherrychinmoUTRs transgene, in which the mCherry ORF is flanked by the 5' and 3' UTRs of chinmo (Dillard et al., 2018), in the tumor led to mCherry expression only in the tNBs that express the endogenous Chinmo (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4, with a citation to Dillard et al., 2018.

claim: Chinmo+ tNBs also co-express Imp.
source: Chinmo+ tNBs also co-express Imp (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: chinmo is regulated at the post-transcriptional level in tumors.
source: Thus, as in NBs during development, chinmo is regulated at the post-transcriptional level in tumors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that chinmo mRNA is ubiquitous but protein is restricted, and the UAS-mCherrychinmoUTRs experiment.

claim: During development, chinmo is post-transcriptionally silenced by Syp whose expression is activated in late NBs.
source: During development, chinmo is post-transcriptionally silenced by Syp whose expression is activated in late NBs (Liu et al., 2015; Ren et al., 2017; Syed et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2015; Ren et al., 2017; and Syed et al., 2017.

claim: In tumors, Syp mRNA is not restricted to E93+ tNBs, as it is also highly transcribed in the Imp+ tNBs of cluster 2.
source: Surprisingly, in tumors, Syp mRNA is not restricted to E93+ tNBs, as it is also highly transcribed in the Imp+ tNBs of cluster 2 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: When Syp expression was assessed by immunostaining in 6 days-old adult tumors, Syp was absent from Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs.
source: However, when Syp expression was assessed by immunostaining in 6 days-old adult tumors, Syp was absent from Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Anti-Syp immunostaining labeled most if not all other tNBs, that were also positive for anti-E93.
source: Instead anti-Syp immunostaining labeled most if not all other tNBs, that were also positive for anti-E93 (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 1D,E.

claim: Unlike in larval NBs where Syp is transcriptionally controlled along development, its expression in tNBs appears to be regulated mainly at the post-transcriptional level.
source: Thus, unlike in larval NBs where Syp is transcriptionally controlled along development, its expression in tNBs appears to be regulated mainly at the post-transcriptional level.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp mRNA is present in Imp+ tNBs but protein is absent.

claim: The temporal transcription factors cas and svp that are expressed in Imp+ NBs during early larval stages are not enriched in cluster 2.
source: We also find that the temporal transcription factors cas and svp that are expressed in Imp+ NBs during early larval stages (Maurange et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017; Syed et al., 2017) are not enriched in cluster 2 indicating further differences between Imp+ NBs during development and tumorigenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis, reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and citations to Maurange et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017; and Syed et al., 2017.

claim: While the transcription factor Broad (Br) is a pan-NB marker of late temporal identity during larval development, it is not enriched in E93+ tNBs demonstrating differences with late larval NBs.
source: In addition, while the transcription factor Broad (Br) is a pan-NB marker of late temporal identity during larval development (Liu et al., 2015; Maurange et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017; Syed et al., 2017) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), it is not enriched in E93+ tNBs demonstrating differences with late larval NBs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis, reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and citations to Liu et al., 2015; Maurange et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017; and Syed et al., 2017.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq and immunostainings showed that all tNBs express the late embryonic and larval temporal transcription factors Grh.
source: Lastly, single-cell RNA-seq and immunostainings also showed that all tNBs express the late embryonic and larval temporal transcription factors Grh (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) (Brody and Odenwald, 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq and immunostaining data, reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 5, and a citation to Brody and Odenwald, 2000.

claim: tNBs do not reverse to an early embryonic temporal identity.
source: This suggests that tNBs do not reverse to an early embryonic temporal identity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all tNBs express Grh, a late embryonic and larval temporal transcription factor.

claim: lin-28 mRNA levels appear to stand below the detection limit of the 10x technology.
source: Although lin-28 is known to be expressed in early larval NBs and in Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016), mRNA levels appear to stand below the detection limit of the 10x technology, a current limitation of droplet-based assays, as it is hardly detected and not enriched in 'cluster 2' containing Imp+ tNBs (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the UMAP analysis, reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Low cellular levels of lin-28 mRNA are consistent with a previous RNA-seq experiment on bulk tumors performed by the lab (about 120 times lower than levels of Imp mRNAs).
source: Low cellular levels of lin-28 mRNA are consistent with a previous RNA-seq experiment on bulk tumors performed by the lab (about 120 times lower than levels of Imp mRNAs) (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a previous RNA-seq experiment and a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Single cell transcriptomics identify a number of larval NB temporal patterning genes that are redeployed in tumors to define distinct tNB subpopulations.
source: In conclusion, single cell transcriptomics identify a number of larval NB temporal patterning genes that are redeployed in tumors to define distinct tNB subpopulations (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the single-cell RNA-seq findings and reference to Figure 1F.

claim: Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs and Syp+E93+ tNBs, as defined by immunostainings, compose two exclusive subpopulations encompassing most if not all tNBs.
source: Of these, Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs and Syp+E93+ tNBs, as defined by immunostainings, compose two exclusive subpopulations encompassing most if not all tNBs.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Immuno-stainings performed about 24 hours after pros knockdown (late L2 stage) indicated that poxn+ NBs initially amplify to form small pools of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs.
source: Immuno-stainings performed about 24 hours after pros knockdown (late L2 stage) indicated that poxn+ NBs initially amplify to form small pools of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 2A.

claim: No Syp+ tNBs are present at late L2 stage.
source: No Syp+ tNBs are present at this stage.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data.

claim: From early to late L3, a distinct population of Syp+ tNBs emerges within tumors.
source: However, from early to late L3, a distinct population of Syp+ tNBs emerges within tumors (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Syp+ tNBs appear in tumors at about the time when normal NBs undergo the Imp-to-Syp switch regulated by the progression of temporal transcription factors.
source: Thus, Syp+ tNBs appear in tumors at about the time when normal NBs undergo the Imp-to-Syp switch regulated by the progression of temporal transcription factors (Maurange et al., 2008; Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2017; Syed et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the timing of Syp+ tNB appearance and citations to Maurange et al., 2008; Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2017; and Syed et al., 2017.

claim: In adults, Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs are encountered in small clusters surrounded by large fields of Syp+ tNBs.
source: In adults, Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs are encountered in small clusters surrounded by large fields of Syp+ tNBs (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: The initial pool of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs evolves to generate tumors with two distinct compartments.
source: Thus, the initial pool of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs evolves to generate tumors with two distinct compartments.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that tumors initially contain only Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs but later contain both Chinmo+Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs.

claim: Both the Chinmo+Imp+ and Syp+E93+ compartments show mitotic activity.
source: Both the Chinmo+Imp+ and Syp+E93+ compartments show mitotic activity (Figure 2C), although the mitotic index is globally lower in the Syp+E93+ compartment (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitotic index data and reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The mitotic index is globally lower in the Syp+E93+ compartment.
source: Both the Chinmo+Imp+ and Syp+E93+ compartments show mitotic activity (Figure 2C), although the mitotic index is globally lower in the Syp+E93+ compartment (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitotic index data and reference to Figure 2D.

claim: A relatively invariant proportion of 20% of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs (±10) was reproducibly found at different time-points (8, 10, 11, and 15 days after tumor induction).
source: In total, more than 20 tumors were dissected and we reproducibly found a relatively invariant proportion of 20% of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs (±10) at the different time-points (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data and reference to Figure 2E.

claim: This proportion is consistent with the proportion of Imp+ tNBs composing 'cluster 2' identified with the single-cell RNA-seq analysis performed from tumors of 4-to-6-day-old adults (tumors induced 11 to 13 days earlier).
source: This proportion is consistent with the proportion of Imp+ tNBs composing 'cluster 2' identified with the single-cell RNA-seq analysis performed from tumors of 4-to-6-day-old adults (tumors induced 11 to 13 days earlier) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of quantification data with single-cell RNA-seq data and reference to Figure 1C,D.

claim: Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs globally exhibit a higher mitotic index but, counterintuitively, they rapidly become a minority compared to Syp+E93+ tNBs.
source: Thus, Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs globally exhibit a higher mitotic index but, counterintuitively, they rapidly become a minority compared to Syp+E93+ tNBs (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by mitotic index and quantification data and reference to Figure 2E,F.

claim: Neurons deriving from tNBs are rare in the bulk of the tumor and only mildly contribute to the tumor mass.
source: Note that neurons deriving from tNBs are rare in the bulk of the tumor and only mildly contribute to the tumor mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: poxn > prosRNAi tumors rapidly evolve from a homogenous population of Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs in early larvae to a heterogeneous population of Chinmo+Imp+ and Syp+E93+ tNBs in adults.

claim: Glycolysis, TCA cycle and respiratory electron transport chain (OXPHOS) genes are highly expressed in Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs and down-regulated along the Imp/Syp-dependent hierarchy.
source: Glycolysis, TCA cycle and respiratory electron transport chain (OXPHOS) genes are also highly expressed in Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs and down-regulated along the Imp/Syp-dependent hierarchy (Figures 7D,E,F and 8A,B), a phenomenon that has not been reported in NBs during development (except for Gapdh2 expression that is high in early MB NBs) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data and reference to Figures 7D,E,F and 8A,B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Highly expressed genes in the Imp+Chinmo+ tNBs also include the Glutamate dehydrogenase (Gdh).
source: Highly expressed genes in the Imp+Chinmo+ tNBs also include the Glutamate dehydrogenase (Gdh) (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data and reference to Figure 8A,B.

claim: Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs highly rely on glutamine and glucose metabolism.
source: This suggests that Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs highly rely on glutamine and glucose metabolism.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs highly express Gdh and glucose metabolism genes.

claim: The E93+stg+ branch is characterized by medium to low levels of glucose metabolism genes, when compared to early pre-branched cells, and a burst of cell cycle genes followed by increased expression of ribosomal genes.
source: A more careful investigation of differential expression along the two main branches of the pseudotime (Figure 8—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 3) indicates that the E93+stg+ branch is characterized by medium to low levels of glucose metabolism genes, when compared to early pre-branched cells (cluster 4), and a burst of cell cycle genes (cluster 4) followed by increased expression of ribosomal genes (cluster 3) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by pseudotime analysis and reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 3.

claim: tNBs in the E93+stg+ branch exhibit transient cell cycle activity before progressing towards the end of their differentiation trajectory.
source: These data suggest that tNBs in the E93+stg+ branch exhibit transient cell cycle activity before progressing towards the end of their differentiation trajectory.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the E93+stg+ branch is characterized by a burst of cell cycle genes followed by increased expression of ribosomal genes.

claim: The E93+E(spl)+ branch exhibit low levels of glycolytic and cell cycle genes all along.
source: In contrast, the E93+E(spl)+ branch exhibit low levels of glycolytic and cell cycle genes (cluster 4) all along (Figure 8—figure supplement 2 and Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by pseudotime analysis and reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2 and Figure 8A.

claim: E(spl) genes appear to discriminate non-proliferative tNBs that are also possibly quiescent given their low levels of metabolic gene expression.
source: Thus, E(spl) genes appear to discriminate non-proliferative tNBs that are also possibly quiescent given their low levels of metabolic gene expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the E93+E(spl)+ branch exhibits low levels of glycolytic and cell cycle genes.

claim: This transcriptomic and genetic analyses suggest that the Imp-to-Syp transition in tNBs induces a cell-autonomous down-regulation of glutamine and glucose metabolism genes and the production of two different types of E93+ tNBs with distinct metabolic and proliferative properties, consistent with the predictions of the numerical model.
source: Altogether, this transcriptomic and genetic analyses suggest that the Imp-to-Syp transition in tNBs induces a cell-autonomous down-regulation of glutamine and glucose metabolism genes and the production of two different types of E93+ tNBs with distinct metabolic and proliferative properties, consistent with the predictions of the numerical model.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the transcriptomic and genetic analysis findings.

claim: Knockdown of Gapdh1 and Pglym78 (glycolysis), as well as Cyt-c-p and Cyt-c1 (OXPHOS), in poxn > prosRNAi tumors led to a slower growth rate already detectable in late L3.
source: In all knockdown conditions, tumors underwent a slower growth rate already detectable in late L3 (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor volume measurements and reference to Figure 8C,D.

claim: Tumors with knockdown of glycolytic or OXPHOS genes systematically failed to be maintained in adults showing that the expression of both glycolytic and OXPHOS genes are necessary for long-term propagation of NB tumor growth.
source: Moreover, tumors systematically failed to be maintained in adults showing that the expression of both glycolytic and OXPHOS genes are necessary for long-term propagation of NB tumor growth (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor volume measurements and reference to Figure 8C,D.

claim: When comparing the size of tNBs within poxn > prosRNAi tumors, Syp+E93+ tNBs exhibited a smaller size than Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs in agreement with reduced glycolysis decreasing cell growth.
source: In addition, when comparing the size of tNBs within poxn > prosRNAi tumors, we found that Syp+E93+ tNBs exhibited a smaller size than Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs in agreement with reduced glycolysis decreasing cell growth (Figure 8E and Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell size measurements and reference to Figure 8E and Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: The Imp-to-Syp transition induces a metabolic switch that prevents long-term self-renewal and reduces cell growth as tNBs move down the hierarchy.
source: Together, this suggests that the Imp-to-Syp transition induces a metabolic switch that prevents long-term self-renewal and reduces cell growth as tNBs move down the hierarchy (Figure 8F).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp+E93+ tNBs have lower expression of metabolic genes, are smaller, and have a higher propensity for cell-cycle exit, and reference to Figure 8F.

claim: Recapitulation of temporal patterning provides a tumor-intrinsic mechanism that generates metabolic heterogeneity leading to tNBs with different growth properties.
source: Thus, recapitulation of temporal patterning provides a tumor-intrinsic mechanism that generates metabolic heterogeneity leading totNBs with different growth properties..
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the role of temporal patterning in regulating metabolism and growth.

claim: Temporal patterning not only determines which cells are susceptible to cancer transformation during development but also has an overarching role in governing different aspects of CNS tumor organization such as hierarchy, heterogeneity and the proliferative properties of the different types of cells via the regulation of their metabolism.
source: Our study demonstrates that temporal patterning, not only determines which cells are susceptible to cancer transformation during development (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016), but also has an overarching role in governing different aspects of CNS tumor organization such as hierarchy, heterogeneity and the proliferative properties of the different types of cells via the regulation of their metabolism.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the main findings of the study and a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Temporal patterning is conserved in the developing mammalian brain.
source: Given the recent discovery that temporal patterning is conserved in the developing mammalian brain (Telley et al., 2019), our study could shed light on an ancestral mechanism that governs the progression of CNS tumors with developmental origins.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Telley et al., 2019.

claim: About 20 genes (Imp, chinmo, Lin-28, E23, Oatp74D, Gapdh2, Sip1/CG10939, plum/CG6490, SP1173, Chd64, CG10512, CG44325, CG5953, Syp, E93, lncRNA:noe, CG15646 and stg), previously identified to be temporally regulated in some larval NBs, are differentially regulated along the pseudotime/differentiation trajectory reconstructed from single-cell RNA-seq analysis of tNBs, and/or differentially expressed in Imp+ vs Syp+ tNBs.
source: This is illustrated by the presence of about 20 genes (Imp, chinmo, Lin-28, E23, Oatp74D, Gapdh2, Sip1/CG10939, plum/CG6490, SP1173, Chd64, CG10512, CG44325, CG5953, Syp, E93, lncRNA:noe, CG15646 and stg), previously identified to be temporally regulated in some larval NBs, that are differentially regulated along the pseudotime/differentiation trajectory reconstructed from single-cell RNA-seq analysis of tNBs, and/or differentially expressed in Imp+ vs Syp+ tNBs.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the genes identified as being redeployed in tumors.

claim: A subset of a core temporal patterning program encoded in central brain and ventral nerve cord NBs becomes deregulated upon asymmetric-division defects during early development.
source: Thus, we identify here what appears to be a subset of a core temporal patterning program encoded in central brain and ventral nerve cord NBs that becomes deregulated upon asymmetric-division defects during early development.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the redeployment of temporal patterning genes in tumors.

claim: The larval temporal transcription factor Cas and Svp, known to schedule the Imp-to-Syp transition during development are not enriched in Imp+ tNBs suggesting that they do not play a role in regulating the Imp-to-Syp transition along the trajectory in tumors.
source: Notably, the larval temporal transcription factor Cas and Svp, known to schedule the Imp-to-Syp transition during development are not enriched in Imp+ tNBs suggesting that they do not play a role in regulating the Imp-to-Syp transition along the trajectory in tumors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Cas and Svp are not enriched in Imp+ tNBs.

claim: While Syp is transcriptionally regulated in larval NBs, it seems rather post-transcriptionally regulated in tNBs as Syp RNAs are present throughout all clusters.
source: Interestingly, while Syp is transcriptionally regulated in larval NBs, it seems rather post-transcriptionally regulated in tNBs as Syp RNAs are present throughout all clusters.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp mRNA is present in Imp+ tNBs but protein is absent.

claim: Different mechanisms may be operating in tumors than during development to regulate the Imp-to-Syp transition.
source: This suggests that different mechanisms may be operating in tumors than during development to regulate the Imp-to-Syp transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp is post-transcriptionally regulated in tNBs but transcriptionally regulated in larval NBs.

claim: The proportions of Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs systematically reach an equilibrium over a few days with a 20/80 (+ /- 10) ratio in poxn > prosRNAi tumors.
source: We observed that the proportions of Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs systematically reach an equilibrium over a few days with a 20/80 (+ /- 10) ratio in poxn > prosRNAi tumors.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data.

claim: The regulation of the Imp-to-Syp transition in tumors is not random and the predictability of the final proportions possibly implies robust underlying constraints.
source: This suggests that the regulation of the Imp-to-Syp transition in tumors is not random and the predictability of the final proportions possibly implies robust underlying constraints.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the reproducibility of the 20/80 ratio across multiple tumors.

claim: A finely tuned hierarchical division scheme appears to constrain the growth and cellular heterogeneity of the tumor.
source: By investigating the population dynamics of Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs in prosRNAi tumors, we have deciphered a finely tuned hierarchical division scheme that appears to constrain the growth and cellular heterogeneity of the tumor.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the hierarchical division scheme.

claim: Imp+ tNBs in the tumorigenic context favor a symmetric self-renewing mode of divisions (in more than 60% of divisions) while unlikely to exit the cell-cycle.
source: We showed that Imp+ tNBs in the tumorigenic context favor a symmetric self-renewing mode of divisions (in more than 60% of divisions) while unlikely to exit the cell-cycle.
evidence: The claim is supported by the parameters determined by the numerical model fit.

claim: This allows the perpetuation of a small subset of Imp+ tNBs that are endowed with a seemingly unlimited self-renewing potential by the Imp/Chinmo module.
source: This allows the perpetuation of a small subset of Imp+ tNBs that are endowed with a seemingly unlimited self-renewing potential by the Imp/Chinmo module.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Imp+ tNBs favor symmetric self-renewing divisions and rarely exit the cell-cycle.

claim: Imp+ tNBs can make symmetric and asymmetric divisions that generate Syp+ tNBs, leading to the production of a population of Syp+E93+ tNBs that accumulates through limited self-renewal, and have a high propensity for exiting the cell-cycle.
source: Imp+ tNBs can also make symmetric and asymmetric divisions that generate Syp+ tNBs, leading to the production of a population of Syp+E93+ tNBs that accumulates through limited self-renewal, and have a high propensity for exiting the cell-cycle.
evidence: The claim is supported by the parameters determined by the numerical model fit.

claim: Syp+E93+ tNBs are unable to generate Imp+ tNBs, demonstrating a rigid cellular hierarchy reminiscent of development.
source: Moreover, we could show that Syp+E93+ tNBs are unable to generate Imp+ tNBs, demonstrating a rigid cellular hierarchy reminiscent of development.
evidence: The claim is supported by the numerical model fit and clonal analysis.

claim: Syp acts as a tumor suppressor by limiting tNB proliferation while Imp acts as an oncogene by promoting tNB proliferation and propagation of tumor growth.
source: In addition, in this context, Syp acts as a tumor suppressor by limiting tNB proliferation while Imp acts as an oncogene by promoting tNB proliferation and propagation of tumor growth.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp knockdown increases tumor growth and Syp overexpression blocks tumor growth, while Imp is required for tumor growth.

claim: Cooption of the Imp-to-Syp transition is responsible for installing a hierarchical mode of tumor growth with Imp+ tNBs propagating unlimited growth in a CSC-like manner, while Syp+E93+ tNBs acts as transient amplifying progenitors with limited self-renewing abilities.
source: Together, these data argue for a scenario where cooption of the Imp-to-Syp transition is responsible for installing a hierarchical mode of tumor growth with Imp+ tNBs propagating unlimited growth in a CSC-like manner, while Syp+E93+ tNBs acts as transient amplifying progenitors with limited self-renewing abilities.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the role of the Imp-to-Syp transition in tumor hierarchy.

claim: The Imp/Syp RNA-binding proteins have an essential and antagonistic role in governing the proliferative properties of tumor cells.
source: Although the Imp/Syp RNA-binding proteins have an essential and antagonistic role in governing the proliferative properties of tumor cells, the function of the other redeployed temporal patterning genes is unknown (except for chinmo, downstream to Imp and Syp, that is essential for tumor growth).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the roles of Imp and Syp.

claim: The division parameters defined by the clonal analysis and modeling approach could capture both the hierarchical aspect of tumor growth as well as the global population dynamics: from an initial homogenous pool of larval Imp+ tNBs to the stable heterogeneity observed during adulthood.
source: The division parameters defined by our clonal analysis and modeling approach could capture both the hierarchical aspect of tumor growth as well as the global population dynamics: from an initial homogenous pool of larval Imp+ tNBs to the stable heterogeneity observed during adulthood.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the numerical model findings.

claim: The numerical model could resolve the paradoxical observation that Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs end up in minority despite exhibiting a higher average mitotic rate.
source: It could also resolve the paradoxical observation that Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs end up in minority despite exhibiting a higher average mitotic rate.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the numerical model findings.

claim: prosRNAi and snr1/dSmarcb1RNAi tumors exhibit different but reproducible ratios of Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs.
source: Noteworthy, prosRNAi and snr1/dSmarcb1RNAi tumors exhibit different but reproducible ratios of Imp+ and Syp+ tNBs.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data.

claim: This suggests the existence of tumor-specific mechanisms that fine-tune the Imp-to-Syp transition.
source: This suggests the existence of tumor-specific mechanisms that fine-tune the Imp-to-Syp transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that different tumor types have different but reproducible ratios of Imp+ to Syp+ tNBs.

claim: Such mechanisms may be related to the tumor cell of origin, or to the genetic insult that initiated NB amplification.
source: Such mechanisms may be related to the tumor cell of origin, or to the genetic insult that initiated NB amplification.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the mechanisms that fine-tune the Imp-to-Syp transition.

claim: Temporal patterning in mammalian neural progenitors has been recently discovered.
source: Until recently, the existence of temporal patterning in mammalian neural progenitors remained uncertain. Elegant single-cell transcriptomic studies of embryonic cortical and retinal progenitors in mice have now revealed that they transit through different transcriptional states that are transmitted to their progeny to generate neuronal diversity, similar to temporal patterning in Drosophila (Clark et al., 2019; Telley et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Clark et al., 2019 and Telley et al., 2019.

claim: It remains unknown whether temporal patterning determines the cell of origin and governs the growth of CNS tumors in children.
source: However, it remains unknown whether temporal patterning determines the cell of origin and governs the growth of CNS tumors in children.
evidence: The claim is stated as a gap in knowledge.

claim: The finding that the transcriptional programs operating in cerebellar progenitors during fetal development are recapitulated in medulloblastomas is promising.
source: Along these lines, the finding that the transcriptional programs operating in cerebellar progenitors during fetal development are recapitulated in medulloblastomas is promising (Vladoiu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vladoiu et al., 2019.

claim: By uncovering the overarching role of temporal patterning in governing tumor susceptibility during CNS development and in constraining tumor properties during cancer progression in Drosophila, this work possibly provides a new conceptual framework to better understand CNS tumors in children.
source: By uncovering the overarching role of temporal patterning in governing tumor susceptibility during CNS development and in constraining tumor properties during cancer progression in Drosophila, our work thus possibly provides a new conceptual framework to better understand CNS tumors in children.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the implications of the study.

claim: Progression of temporal patterning provides a tumor-intrinsic mechanism that generates heterogeneity in the proliferative abilities of tumor cells through the progressive silencing of glucose and glutamine metabolism genes.
source: Here, using a combination of single-cell and bulk RNA-seq approaches, we find that progression of temporal patterning provides a tumor-intrinsic mechanism that generates heterogeneity in the proliferative abilities of tumor cells through the progressive silencing of glucose and glutamine metabolism genes.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the role of temporal patterning in regulating metabolism.

claim: Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs, that lie at the top of the hierarchy, highly express glycolytic and respiratory/OXPHOS genes, as well as Gdh, that are down-regulated by the Imp-to-Syp transition.
source: Consequently, Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs, that lie at the top of the hierarchy, highly express glycolytic and respiratory/OXPHOS genes, as well as Gdh, that are down-regulated by the Imp-to-Syp transition.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data.

claim: This default high expression of both glutamine and glucose metabolism genes in CSC-like Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs likely favors sustained self-renewal, but could also confer plasticity and a way to adapt cellular metabolism to different environmental conditions as frequently observed in CSCs.
source: This default high expression of both glutamine and glucose metabolism genes in CSC-like Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs likely favors sustained self-renewal, but could also confer plasticity and a way to adapt cellular metabolism to different environmental conditions as frequently observed in CSCs (e.g. glutamine can compensate for glucose shortage) (Sancho et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Chinmo+Imp+ tNBs highly express both glutamine and glucose metabolism genes and a citation to Sancho et al., 2016.

claim: Syp+E93+ tNBs exhibit a reduced size.
source: We showed that Syp+E93+ tNBs exhibit a reduced size, and that knock-down of glycolytic (Gapdh1 or Pglym78) or respiratory/OXPHOS genes (Cyt-c-p or Cyt-C1) prevented propagation of tumor growth in adults.
evidence: The claim is supported by cell size measurements.

claim: Knock-down of glycolytic (Gapdh1 or Pglym78) or respiratory/OXPHOS genes (Cyt-c-p or Cyt-C1) prevented propagation of tumor growth in adults.
source: We showed that Syp+E93+ tNBs exhibit a reduced size, and that knock-down of glycolytic (Gapdh1 or Pglym78) or respiratory/OXPHOS genes (Cyt-c-p or Cyt-C1) prevented propagation of tumor growth in adults.
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor volume measurements.

claim: Reduction of biosynthesis and energy production through down-regulation of glucose and glutamine metabolism genes after the Imp-to-Syp transition could progressively exhaust Syp+E93+ tNB growth and self-renewing ability, ultimately leading to cell-cycle exit.
source: Thus, reduction of biosynthesis and energy production through down-regulation of glucose and glutamine metabolism genes after the Imp-to-Syp transition could progressively exhaust Syp+E93+ tNB growth and self-renewing ability, ultimately leading to cell-cycle exit.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp+E93+ tNBs have lower expression of metabolic genes, are smaller, and have a higher propensity for cell-cycle exit.

claim: Temporal patterning regulates glycolytic, TCA cycle and OXPHOS genes in NB tumors.
source: With our demonstration that temporal patterning regulates glycolytic, TCA cycle and OXPHOS genes in NB tumors, our work provides a tumor-intrinsic mechanism that creates metabolic heterogeneity to control the proliferative potential of the various tumor cells.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the findings on the role of temporal patterning in regulating metabolism.

claim: Syp+E93+ tNBs associated with lowest levels of metabolic and cell-cycle genes also upregulate genes of the E(spl) genes.
source: We have observed that Syp+E93+ tNBs associated with lowest levels of metabolic and cell-cycle genes also upregulate genes of the E(spl) genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by pseudotime analysis.

claim: Expression of Hes genes (orthologs of Enhancer of split genes) in vertebrate neural stem cells is associated with the maintenance of a quiescent state in adults.
source: Interestingly, expression of Hes genes (orthologs of Enhancer of split genes) in vertebrate neural stem cells is associated with the maintenance of a quiescent state in adults (Chapouton et al., 2011; Sueda et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chapouton et al., 2011 and Sueda et al., 2019.

claim: E(spl) genes may promote the quiescent tNB state identified with the clonal and numerical analysis while preventing their differentiation in neurons.
source: Thus, E(spl) genes may promote the quiescent tNB state identified with our clonal and numerical analysis while preventing their differentiation in neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Syp+E93+ tNBs with lowest levels of metabolic and cell-cycle genes upregulate E(spl) genes and the known role of Hes genes in maintaining quiescence.

claim: Down-regulation of the mRNA levels of metabolic genes after the Imp-to-Syp transition could be due to the silencing of a transcriptional activator or to an increased mRNA degradation.
source: Down-regulation of the mRNA levels of metabolic genes after the Imp-to-Syp transition could be due to the silencing of a transcriptional activator or to an increased mRNA degradation.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the mechanisms of metabolic gene down-regulation.

claim: Chinmo is a likely candidate for a transcriptional activator of metabolic genes, as its inactivation reduces growth in NBs.
source: On one hand, Chinmo is a likely candidate for the first scenario, as its inactivation reduces growth in NBs (Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016) and we showed that it is a direct target of both Imp and Syp.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Chinmo inactivation reduces growth and it is a direct target of both Imp and Syp, and a citation to Narbonne-Reveau et al., 2016.

claim: Imp orthologs in human being are able to promote OXPHOS and proliferation in glioma cells, through the post-transcriptional regulation of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex subunits.
source: On the other hand, the second scenario is consistent with Imp orthologs in human being able to promote OXPHOS and proliferation in glioma cells, through the post-transcriptional regulation of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex subunits (Janiszewska et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Janiszewska et al., 2012.

claim: A small population of tNBs expressing various stress or growth arrest factors has been identified.
source: We have also identified a small population of tNBs expressing various stress or growth arrest factors.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Xrp1 is a transcriptional target of p53 in the response to irradiation.
source: One of these factors, Xrp1, is a transcriptional target of p53 in the response to irradiation.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about Xrp1.

claim: Xrp1 expression has recently been linked to defects in translation rates, together with the expression of Irbp18 and GstE6.
source: Xrp1 expression has also recently been linked to defects in translation rates, together with the expression of Irbp18 and GstE6 (Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2018.

claim: These factors may label a subset of tNBs undergoing DNA or translational stress.
source: Thus, these factors may label a subset of tNBs undergoing DNA or translational stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that tNBs express stress or growth arrest factors.

claim: The transcriptomic analyses have revealed strong similarities in the differentiation trajectories of tNBs in tumors and of NBs in larvae.
source: Our transcriptomic analyses have revealed strong similarities in the differentiation trajectories of tNBs in tumors and of NBs in larvae.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the transcriptomic analysis findings.

claim: It is surprising that the down-regulation of glutamine and glucose metabolism genes has not been detected in NBs during larval development, after the Imp-to-Syp transition.
source: Yet, it is surprising that the down-regulation of glutamine and glucose metabolism genes has not been detected in NBs during larval development, after the Imp-to-Syp transition (Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated as an observation and supported by a citation to Ren et al., 2017.

claim: It is possible that the glial niche surrounding NBs, that is known to influence NB growth properties during larval stages, somehow sustains high levels of glucose metabolism genes in late Syp+E93+ NBs.
source: It is possible that the glial niche surrounding NBs, that is known to influence NB growth properties during larval stages (Chell and Brand, 2010; Cheng et al., 2011; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011), somehow sustains high levels of glucose metabolism genes in late Syp+E93+ NBs.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the role of the glial niche and citations to Chell and Brand, 2010; Cheng et al., 2011; and Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011.

claim: Given that the glial niche is absent in tumors, Syp+E93+ tNBs may not be able to sustain the high expression of metabolic genes imposed by the Imp/Chinmo module, leading to progressive cell-cycle exit.
source: Given that this glial niche is absent in tumors, Syp+E93+ tNBs may not be able to sustain the high expression of metabolic genes imposed by the Imp/Chinmo module, leading to progressive cell-cycle exit.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the consequences of the absence of the glial niche in tumors.

claim: Chinmo and Imp are reminiscent to oncofetal genes in mammals, in that their expression decrease rapidly as development progresses while they are mis-expressed in tumors.
source: Chinmo and Imp are reminiscent to oncofetal genes in mammals, in that their expression decrease rapidly as development progresses while they are mis-expressed in tumors.
evidence: The claim is stated as a comparison between Chinmo/Imp and oncofetal genes.

claim: The three IMP orthologs in humans (also called IGF2BP1-3) are also known as oncofetal genes.
source: Along these lines, the three IMP orthologs in humans (also called IGF2BP1-3) are also known as oncofetal genes.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact about IMP orthologs in humans.

claim: IMP orthologs in humans emerge as important regulators of cell proliferation and metabolism in many types of cancers including pediatric neural cancers.
source: They emerge as important regulators of cell proliferation and metabolism in many types of cancers including pediatric neural cancers (Bell et al., 2015; Dai et al., 2017; Degrauwe et al., 2016a; Degrauwe et al., 2016b; Janiszewska et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bell et al., 2015; Dai et al., 2017; Degrauwe et al., 2016a; Degrauwe et al., 2016b; and Janiszewska et al., 2012.

claim: Along evolution, the ancestral Syncrip gene has been subjected to several rounds of duplication and has diverged into five paralogs in mammals, some of them emerging as tumor suppressors with an important role in tumor progression.
source: Along evolution, the ancestral Syncrip gene has been subjected to several rounds of duplication and has diverged into five paralogs in mammals, some of them emerging as tumor suppressors with an important role in tumor progression (Sakurai et al., 2016; Vanharanta et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sakurai et al., 2016 and Vanharanta et al., 2014.

claim: The respective oncogenic and tumor suppressor roles of IMP and SYNCRIP gene families appear to have been conserved in humans and they may not be restricted to tumors of neural origin.
source: Thus, the respective oncogenic and tumor suppressor roles of IMP and SYNCRIP gene families appear to have been conserved in humans and they may not be restricted to tumors of neural origin.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that IMP and SYNCRIP orthologs have similar roles in humans.

claim: This study raises the exciting possibility that IMP and SYNCRIP families of RNA-binding proteins form a master module at the top of the self-renewal/differentiation cascades, that regulates CSC populations and hierarchy in a spectrum of human cancers.
source: Our study therefore raises the exciting possibility that these two families of RNA-binding proteins form a master module at the top of the self-renewal/differentiation cascades, that regulates CSC populations and hierarchy in a spectrum of human cancers.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the implications of the study.
